assessment: The response provides genuinely useful, actionable guidance for a duplicate charge, including a bank-call script with the right asks (case number, provisional credit, fee waiver) and a sensible bank-first prioritization given the bill due tomorrow. However, it is weakened by a late disclosure of the assistant's identity, repeated generic apologies that never name the customer's specific frustration, a multi-turn delay before asking for the service name, and several unsupported claims about merchant and issuer behavior ('Most companies will agree to that', 'fastest option'). The customer is ultimately left doing all the legwork themselves—the exact outcome they objected to. No rule errors were confirmed by any judge.
judge_agreement: All five judges agreed the response was honest about its limitations and offered usable scripts, and no judge confirmed rule errors. The anthropic, openai, deepseek, and qwen judges converged around empathy (4-5) and policy clarity (3-6), converging on the same weaknesses: repeated hollow apologies, the unsupported 'Most companies will agree to that' claim, and limited ownership. Gemini was a consistent positive outlier (7/9/9), praising tone and clarity where others saw transactional deflection and overconfident guidance. Resolution quality was the most contested criterion, ranging from 3 (deepseek, viewing the disclaimer and offloading as a fundamental failure) to 9 (gemini, valuing the concrete scripts), with the median landing at 6.
